newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks drift in positive territory.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks drift in positive territory.

text.p: Tokyo stocks drifted in positive territory in mid-morning Friday trade, brokers said, supported by buying of shares of firms oriented toward domestic demand, brokers said. The fluctuations of the yen against the dollar were keeping investors away from blue chips, they added.
At 0120 GMT, the Nikkei average was up 177.01 points or 0.88 percent at 20,233.32. June Nikkei futures rose 220 to 20,280.
"The yen is a bit weaker now, but until it stabilises, investors will be reluctant to take the risk of buying export-strong blue chips," a foreign brokerage trader said.
Some brokers added the weakening of the yen against the dollar in the morning, after the yen powered past 115 to the dollar in London on Thursday, brightened market sentiment slightly.
But many investors were taking a wait-and-see stance ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting scheduled for next week, with the outcome possibly resulting in higher U.S. interest rates.
Turnover was a modest 225 million shares by midday, with winners beating losers 816 to 248, while 179 issues were unchanged.
The broader TOPIX rose 11.32 points or 0.76 percent to end the two-hour session at 1,500.50. The Nikkei 300 was up 2.04 points or 0.71 percent at 290.49.

"The Nikkei average has been supported greatly by buying in sectors that have lagged behind and shares of firms which benefit from domestic demand, after exporter shares started slowing. Trade this morning was just another example of that sort of buying," a "Big Four" broker said.
NTT's shares hit a fresh calendar year high in the morning of 1.07 million yen. They stood at 1.06 million by midday, up by 30,000.
Brokers said however that further gains due to such buying were limited and that blue-chips would need to stage a comeback for the Nikkei average to rise far past 20,000.
The steady stream of corporate earnings results and forecasts was also being assessed by investors. Tsutsumi Jewelry Co Ltd slumped on a bearish forecast, losing 110 yen to 2,620 by midday.

Shares of Japan Digital Laboratory Co Ltd rose for a second day, fuelled by a bright business outlook. Japan Digital rose 150 yen or 7.89 percent to 2,050, becoming the largest percentage gainer on the first section of the bourse.
The gaining sectors were led by warehouses, fisheries, railway/bus, insurance and mining. The retreaters were headed by communications, real estate, credit/lease, chemicals and air transport.
